acceptanceScope: Local assembly at original torso service station: completed legs/base/rings present, side shells/neck absent. Reuses original power_support material/path; checks all added material/electronics/short J4 receivers. DFR and its pre-soldered leads are deliberately loose until four body screws close. Not whole flexible wiring or physical strength acceptance.
assemblySequence: With the carrier detached, seat the OpenRB on its four bosses and tighten four M2x6 TAP screws from +X. The 3mm diameter, 40mm driver receiving shafts are clear.
Pre-solder the three labelled DFR VIN/GND/VOUT pad leads while the board is free. Keep this board loose beside the carrier; do not retain it yet. Prepare the OpenRB J4 leads before body closure.
At the original torso service station, completed legs/base/rings are present and side shells/neck are absent. Move carrier plus OpenRB and local J4 leads from -X28 to the four original body mounts.
Tighten the four original M2x10 TAP body screws before installing the DFR. Retaining the DFR prematurely blocks the two lower screw driver shafts by about 8.06mm3 each.

With the liner strips not yet installed, slide the prewired DFR through the open +X end from +45mm with the board 0.8mm below its final seat, then lift 0.8mm to the final seat. Both bench and installed-body paths were checked.

Hold the seated board and slide two 26x2x1mm insulating strips through the open end at Y=+/-7mm, between the three solder-pad lead exits. Then thread two narrow removable ties through the four side slots and retain the board along its outer edges. Keep ties off components, solder pads and the central J4 wire corridor. Four 4.8x1.2mm free-end passage receivers were checked; flexible tightening is a physical assembly step.
Keep the pad-end exits open and inspect insulation before the remaining original body closure steps. Complete supply distribution and head USB routing are outside this local assembly receipt.
remaining: Complete internal Pi USB route and full motor/power harness integration.
Actual supply wire selection, termination/distribution and loaded commissioning.
Printed strength, liner/tie retention and physical fit.
